1493.input_message: Notice what it feels like to see other people smoke and choose not to smoke. Notice what thoughts or emotions come up. Allow them to come and go. They will pass and so will this urge.
1493.explanation: This Acceptance message is similar to the participant's past low-rated Acceptance message about letting urges pass, which they found unhelpful for coping but slightly for quitting; they prefer Distraction types.

1492.input_message: Just because other people are smoking, doesn't mean you have to. Practice allowing this urge to be present for 5 minutes. When it passes, give yourself credit.
1492.explanation: As an acceptance message, aligns with past low-rated acceptance (very poor content, low coping), but theme of social smoking echoes high-rated distraction message, leading to moderate ratings overall.

1494.input_message: Life can get you really stressed out, but turning to cigs isn't the answer. Call or text family and friends instead. Ask them to help you stay on track.
1494.explanation: Participant favors practical, empowering distraction messages involving social support or alternatives to triggers, as seen in high ratings for avoiding smoke and countering thoughts; this aligns with her moderate motivation and somewhat supportive network, unlike lower-rated vague escapes.

1495.input_message: Notice how stress and anxiety may pull you and make you want to smoke. Just notice this. You can choose to just notice and not smoke.
1495.explanation: This direct Acceptance message about noticing urges and choosing not to smoke is similar to the participant's positively rated Acceptance message on confidence with urges, fitting their high motivation and low emotional barriers.

1497.input_message: You were often stressed in this location and this might trigger urges. What can you do to reduce your stress here? If you can avoid this place until things settle down, then do.
1497.explanation: Distraction message similar to past high-rated avoidance strategy (e.g., avoiding smokers), aligns with participant's motivation and low emotional issues; expects strong positive response.

1496.input_message: Try to stop smoking by setting yourself a rule. For example, "IF I am tempted, THEN I will chew on some mints" - make your own rule that will work for you.
1496.explanation: This Distraction message offers practical if-then strategy similar to past highly-rated Distraction messages like avoiding triggers or using mantras, which the participant rated Good/Very good and Very/Extremely helpful.

1498.input_message: What can you do right now to break the automatic habit of smoking when you are here? Pause. Close your eyes. And take 10 slow breaths.
1498.explanation: Participant rates practical acceptance messages highly, similar to the positive past acceptance rating; breathing technique aligns with motivation and low emotional barriers.

1499.input_message: A funny thing about people is that we tend to believe what we tell ourselves. So make sure that whatever else happens today, tell yourself "I can, and I will stick to not smoking!"
1499.explanation: The message uses positive self-talk similar to past Distraction messages rated highly (e.g., mantra example), aligning with participant's motivation and preference for Distraction over some Acceptance types.
